candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema ruled from the bench on November 20 to block construction of President Trump's proposed 250-foot memorial arch while Arlington County's lawsuit proceeds, according to plaintiffs' lawyers. The injunction has no specified expiration date. It is separate from a Washington federal court's temporary restraining order, extended on November 18 through December 3.
candidates.title: Second federal judge blocks construction of Trump's proposed memorial arch

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed sharply lower on November 20. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, the Nasdaq composite dropped 5.3% to 22,617.73, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.9% to 48,147.33. The S&P 500 finished more than 10% below its October 6 record and lost 8.6% for the week. The Nasdaq turned negative for the year.
candidates.title: S&P 500 closes in correction as Nasdaq falls 5.3%

candidates.summary: At a November 20 White House news conference, President Trump threatened a large tax on U.S. companies that build artificial intelligence data centers abroad. He said he had not yet told his staff about the proposal. No tax rate, enforcement mechanism or implementation timetable was provided; the remarks did not establish an enacted tax or prohibition.
candidates.title: Trump proposes tax penalties for U.S. companies building AI data centers abroad

candidates.summary: COP31 negotiations in Antalya continued beyond their scheduled November 20 finish without agreement. Fossil fuels and climate finance remained disputed. The latest draft political decision, published November 19, omitted fossil fuels and did not reiterate the earlier commitment to transition away from them. That text remained a negotiating draft, not an adopted agreement.
candidates.title: COP31 talks run into overtime with fossil fuels and financing unresolved

candidates.summary: President Trump said at his November 20 White House news conference that Iran wanted an agreement to end hostilities but had not offered terms acceptable to him. AP also reported, citing an unnamed Middle Eastern diplomat, that Gulf Arab states were using existing communications channels to seek a partial solution involving shipping access through the Strait of Hormuz and limited sanctions relief. No agreement was announced.
candidates.title: Trump says Iran's proposed terms remain unacceptable as Gulf mediation continues
